wa_burnt_boot_peak_north_ridge.beta: Recorded in a single short first-ascent note by Don Williamson: 'Across the middle fork of the Snoqualmie River, two miles southeast of Big Snow Mountain lies P 6480, now officially Burnt Boot Peak. Bill Bucher, Tom Oas and I climbed a new route, the north ridge. From the base of the steepest part of the ridge, three leads of class five on granite, the last being a very sharp crest, led to easier ground. Three leads of class three and four put us on the summit.' The note records that the only previous ascent found in the summit register was that of a 1963 survey party (the peak's first ascent, via the easier scramble line). No repeat ascents of this line are recorded, suggesting it sees little to no modern traffic.

wa_summit_chief_mountain_north_face.overview: A rarely repeated, sustained alpine ice line up a series of runnels and couloirs just right of the true summit on Summit Chief's north side — Colin Haley called it more sustained ice climbing than almost any other Cascade ice route he had done at the time.
